gap: No result ChatGPT got ties Victron's under-voltage-protection reset to lithium batteries. Victron's own manual says the Blue Smart IP65 resets a tripped UVP on a Li-ion battery and starts charging. Its Li-ion mode also stops at 14.2 V with float disabled, and Victron warns not to charge Li-ion below 0 °C but describes no automatic low-temperature cut-off. So the $160–176 Victron can wake a BMS that has shut off, just like the $83 Redodo 20A and $103 LiTime 20A, while NOCO's only way is Force Mode, which switches its protections off.
standout_why: Victron's cited product page (victronenergy.com/chargers/blue-smart-ip65-charger) already says 'revive deeply discharged batteries with automatic under-voltage protection reset', but it never names lithium or a BMS. The cited spec page shows 14.2 V Li-ion absorption with no float, but says nothing about 0 V or UVP. powergearguide.com warns in general terms about force and recovery modes but names no product. rvpartsgiant.com covers NOCO's 1 V start and 0 V Force Mode but says nothing about Victron or a BMS. clampandcrank.com mentions BMS only in general terms. epicvanlife.com only repeats '0V Activation' from the LiTime product title. The rival pages leave out the manual's Li-ion section, which ties the UVP reset to Li-ion and closes the BMS-wake question for Victron. gearranking.com and solargenadvisor.com would not load (certificate error), so they were not checked.
decides: This confirms that every candidate except NOCO can restart a 12 V LiFePO4 pack whose BMS has shut off from low voltage without bypassing any protection. Our row saying Victron's wake is 'Not stated by the dealer' should change to 'Yes, automatic UVP reset (Victron manual)'. BMS wake therefore no longer separates Victron from Redodo or LiTime. The pick turns on price per amp: Redodo 20A at $82.99 against LiTime 20A at $102.99. NOCO's 0 V route through Force Mode is the weak one, and the NOCO guide's actual text is still unsourced. One caution belongs on the page: none of these chargers is documented to cut off when cold, so for winter charging the low-temperature cut-off has to come from the battery's own BMS.

findings.label: Wakes a lithium battery whose under-voltage protection has tripped
findings.value: Yes, automatic: 'If the charger is connected to a battery where under voltage protection (UVP) has tripped, it will automatically reset UVP and start charging; many other chargers will not recognise a battery in this state.'
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 3. Features
findings.note: From feature item '9. Lithium Ion compatible' in the maker's online manual.

findings.label: Recovery of a battery from 0 V
findings.value: 'The charger will attempt to recharge a severely discharged battery (even down to 0V) with low current and then resume normal charging once the battery voltage has risen sufficiently'
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 3. Features
findings.note: Feature item '13. Recovery function'. The Operation section adds that a test stage ends once a charge pulse lifts the battery above 12.5 V, or after 2 minutes.

findings.label: Li-ion (LiFePO4) mode voltages, 12 V
findings.value: 14.2 V absorption; float N/A; storage 13.5 V. No temperature compensation in Li-ion mode
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 9. Technical specifications
findings.note: In the same manual, the charge-voltage table on the Operation page shows float and storage as 'Disabled' for Li-ion, with fixed absorption as the default. The other models on this page charge to 14.6 V.

findings.label: Current and minimum Li-ion battery size
findings.value: 15 A max, 4 A low-current mode. Minimum Li-ion capacity 30 Ah in max mode (≤0.5C), 8 Ah in low mode. Max battery 150 Ah (≥0.1C)
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 9. Technical specifications
findings.note: The 12/15 row of the spec table.

findings.label: Li-ion charge time, maker's worked example
findings.value: 100 Ah fully discharged battery on a 10 A charger: 9.5 h bulk plus about 0.5 h absorption = 10 h
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 4. Operation (4.5.2 Li-ion based chemistry)
findings.note: Scaling Victron's example to 15 A: 95 Ah ÷ 15 A ≈ 6.3 h bulk + 0.5 h ≈ 6.8 h, which matches our page's 'About 7 h'. This is our arithmetic, not a Victron figure.

findings.label: Low-temperature charging
findings.value: Warning only: 'Do not charge Li-ion batteries if the battery temperature is below 0°C.' The manual describes no automatic low-temperature cut-off
findings.source_title: Victron Blue Smart IP65 Charger (120V) manual, 3. Features
findings.note: The Advanced Configuration page lists no low-temperature cut-off setting either (checked the same day). The rated operating range is -20 to 50 °C, from the spec page.

findings.value: 'can activate lithium battery protected by BMS'; '3-stage Pre-charge/constant current/constant voltage charge algorithm'; 14.6 V, 20 A; 2-year warranty
